h: Wine and spiritual joy and the life of the righteous

p: "בְּחַמְרָא גּוֹ כָסָא, וּמְדָאנֵי אָסָא, לַאֲרוּס וַאֲרוּסָה וְכוּלֵי" – צֵירֵף הַיַּיִן וַהֲדַס;
''With wine in the cup, and bundles of myrtle, for the groom and the bride, etc.'—he paired wine and myrtle;
דְּאָסָא מָצִינוּ (מְגִילָּה יג עַמּוּד א): "הַצַּדִּיקִים שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ הֲדַסִּים",
for with myrtle we find (Megillah 13a): 'the righteous who are called myrtles,'
וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים".
and all Israel possess a share in the World to Come, as it is stated: 'And your people are all righteous.'
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (צג עַמּוּד א):
And in the holy Zohar in this portion (93a):
"וְהָא כַּמָּה חַיָּיבִין אִית בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, כַּמָּה חַטָּאִין וְכַמָּה רְשִׁיעִין וְכוּלֵי,
''Behold, how many sinners exist in Israel, how many transgressors, and how many wicked, etc.,
אֶלָּא וְכוּלֵי, דִּמְקָרְבִין בְּנַיְיהוּ לִתְמַנְיָא יוֹמִין לְקָרְבָּנָא, וְכַד אִתְגְּזַרוּ וְכוּלֵי אִקְרוּן צַדִּיקִים וְכוּלֵי",
except, etc., that they offer their sons on the eighth day as a sacrifice, and once circumcised, etc., they are termed righteous, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (סַנְהֶדְרִין מד עַמּוּד א) עַל הַפָּסוּק "חָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל":
and this is based upon what is written in the Gemara (Sanhedrin 44a) on the verse 'Israel has sinned':
"אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא – יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא;
''Even though he sinned, he remains Israel;
אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרֵי אִינָשֵׁי: אָסָא דְּקָאֵי בֵּינֵי חִילְפֵי, אָסָא שְׁמֵיהּ וְאָסָא קָרוּ לֵיהּ".
Rabbi Abba said: this is what people say: A myrtle standing among thorny willows, its name is myrtle and myrtle they call it.''
וְהוּא, שֶׁכֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל הַתִּינוֹק לִשְׁמוֹנָה שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ וְנַעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי כֵן יִשְׂרָאֵל,
And this means that since the infant is circumcised on the eighth day without conscious choice, becoming a Jew through this,
וְזֶה מוֹרֶה שֶׁקָּשׁוּר בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּרֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה,
it demonstrates that he is bound at the root unto Hashem, blessed be He, in the primordial Thought,
וְכָל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עָלָיו, בֶּאֱמֶת: "רְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנְךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה וְכוּלֵי",
and whatever transpires over him, in truth: 'Our will is to do Your will, and what hinders? The leaven in the dough, etc.,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת יז עַמּוּד א).
as written in (Berakhot 17a).
וְהַיְינוּ מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָאָסָא עוֹמֵד בֵּין הַקּוֹצִים,
And this is because the myrtle stands among thorns,
וְהַיְינוּ עוֹבְדֵי כוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶם בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרַע,
namely the nations who possess evil within their root,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה מִסְתַּעֵף גַּם לְלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָה.
and through this the leaven in the dough branches into the heart of Israel as well.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Lech Lecha 33:379-380 (I 93a): “Rabbi Abba opened and said: “Your people are all righteous,” and so forth. The companions have explained this matter. Why is it written, “Your people are all righteous”? Are all Israel righteous? There are many guilty people among Israel, many sinners and wicked people who transgress the commandments of Torah. Rather, thus it was taught in the mystery of the teaching: Fortunate are Israel, who make a willing offering to the Holy One, blessed be He, bringing their sons at eight days as an offering. When they are circumcised, they enter this good portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: “The righteous is the foundation of the world.” Once they enter this portion of the righteous, they are called righteous: certainly, all of them are righteous.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: פתח רבי אבא ואמר (ישעיהו ס׳:כ״א) ועמך כלם צדיקים וגו'. מלה דא הא אוקמוה חברייא מאי טעמא כתיב ועמך כלם צדיקים, וכי כלהו ישראל צדיקי נינהו. והא כמה חייבין אית בהו בישראל כמה חטאין וכמה רשיעין דעברין על פקודי אורייתא. אלא הכי תנא ברזא דמתניתין. זכאין אנון ישראל דעבדין קרבנא דרעוא לקודשא בריך הוא דמקריבין בנייהו לתמניא יומין לקרבנא, וכד אתגזרו עאלו בהאי חולקא טבא דקודשא בריך הוא דכתיב, (משלי י׳:כ״ה) וצדיק יסוד עולם. כיון דעאלו בהאי חולקא דצדיק אקרון צדיקים, ודאי כלם צדיקים.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 44a: ‘§ When God explained to Joshua the reason for the Jewish people’s defeat at the city of Ai, He said: “Israel has sinned” (Joshua 7:11). Rabbi Abba bar Zavda says: From here it may be inferred that even when the Jewish people have sinned, they are still called “Israel.” Rabbi Abba says: This is in accordance with the adage that people say: Even when a myrtle is found among thorns, its name is myrtle and people call it myrtle.’

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 17a:2: “Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to do Your will. What prevents us? The leaven in the dough and subjection to the kingdoms. May it be Your will to deliver us from their hands, so that we may return to perform the statutes of Your will with a whole heart.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayera 8:12: “This is why the formula [in the blessing of circumcision] is “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb,” apart from the blessing that the father recites. Why does this blessing differ from all the blessings whose formula is “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us”? Because the letter yud has no form of its own: it is included in His essence, beyond the apprehension of human understanding. The commandment of circumcision likewise is holiness from the womb, beyond the apprehension of human understanding. Therefore we bless, “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb”: through circumcision it becomes manifest that Israel are holy from the womb and from birth, beyond the power of service, in a place the power of human service cannot reach. In all the other commandments, however, the holiness is from the person who sanctifies himself through his own power of service. Therefore we bless, “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us.””

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: וְזֶה הוּא שֶׁהַנּוּסַח (מִבִּרְכַּת בְּרִית מִילָה) הוּא: "אֲשֶׁר קִדַּשׁ יְדִיד מִבֶּטֶן", חוּץ מֵהַבְּרָכָה שֶׁהָאָב מְבָרֵךְ; וְלָמָּה נִשְׁתַּנָּה זוֹ הַבְּרָכָה מִכָּל הַבְּרָכוֹת שֶׁהַנּוּסַח הוּא "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ"? אָכֵן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאוֹת יוּ"ד אֵין לָהּ שׁוּם צוּרָה מִצַּד עַצְמָהּ, כִּי הִיא כְּלוּלָה בְּעַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסַת שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם, וּמִצְוַת מִילָה הִיא גַּם כֵּן קְדוּשָּׁה מִבֶּטֶן לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסַת שֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם; לָכֵן מְבָרְכִין "אֲשֶׁר קִדַּשׁ יְדִיד מִבֶּטֶן" – שֶׁבְּמִצְוַת מִילָה מִתְגַּלֶּה שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְדוֹשִׁים הֵם מִבֶּטֶן וּמִלֵּידָה לְמַעְלָה מִכֹּחַ עֲבוֹדָה, בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁלֹּא יַשִּׂיג כֹּחַ עֲבוֹדַת אָדָם; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּכָל שְׁאָר הַמִּצְווֹת, שֶׁהַקְּדוּשָּׁה הִיא מִצַּד הָאָדָם שֶׁמְּקַדֵּשׁ אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ בְּכֹחַ עֲבוֹדָתוֹ, לָכֵן מְבָרְכִינַן "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ".

sourceExcerpt.en: This is why the formula [in the blessing of circumcision] is “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb,” apart from the blessing that the father recites. Why does this blessing differ from all the blessings whose formula is “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us”? Because the letter yud has no form of its own: it is included in His essence, beyond the apprehension of human understanding. The commandment of circumcision likewise is holiness from the womb, beyond the apprehension of human understanding. Therefore we bless, “Who sanctified the beloved one from the womb”: through circumcision it becomes manifest that Israel are holy from the womb and from birth, beyond the power of service, in a place the power of human service cannot reach. In all the other commandments, however, the holiness is from the person who sanctifies himself through his own power of service. Therefore we bless, “Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 1:2: “The preparation for this was the afflictions of Egypt, which began with Isaac’s birth, as the Sages said. Isaac was the first to be born holy, holy from the womb. Abraham, in contrast, recognized his Creator afterward, and therefore is called “the father of a multitude of nations.” The Sages said at the beginning of Chagigah that he was the first of the converts; in Bikkurim they call Abraham the father of converts. Isaac, however, is the father of Israelites. [Therefore they said in Kiddushin concerning Esau: he was an apostate Israelite.] For this reason Isaac was circumcised at eight days, before he knew anything of evil or of choosing good. The matter does not depend on his choice: his very flesh is holy flesh. Accordingly, Torah begins with Isaac, as I have heard many times concerning the precise expression of the Sages in several places, “Moses, from the mouth of Gevurah.” So too the Zohar says that Torah comes from the side of Gevurah, which is Isaac’s level, as is known. Torah is what especially distinguishes the children of Israel, who are holy from the womb. The Sages said, “Even though he has sinned, he is Israel,” unlike the nations of the world.”

sourceExcerpt.he: וְהַהֲכָנָה לָזֶה — יִסּוּרֵי מִצְרַיִם, וְהֵם הִתְחִילוּ מִלֵּידַת יִצְחָק, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה [סֵדֶר עוֹלָם רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ג׳]. כִּי יִצְחָק הוּא הָרִאשׁוֹן הַנּוֹלָד מִלֵּדָה, מִבֶּטֶן, קָדוֹשׁ מֵרֶחֶם; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן אַבְרָהָם, אַחַר כָּךְ הִכִּיר בּוֹרְאוֹ, וּלְכָךְ נִקְרָא: "אַב הֲמוֹן גּוֹיִם" [בְּרֵאשִׁית י״ז:ה׳]. וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק קַמָּא דְּחַגִיגָה (ג׳ עַמּוּד א׳) שֶׁהָיָה תְּחִלָּה לַגֵּרִים, וּבְמַסֶּכֶת בִּכּוּרִים (פֶּרֶק א׳ מִשְׁנָה ד׳) שֶׁאַבְרָהָם אֲבִי הַגֵּרִים; מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְחָק הוּא אָב לְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים [וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (י״ח עַמּוּד ב׳) עַל עֵשָׂו: יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר הָיָה], וּלְכָךְ נִמּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה טֶרֶם יָדַע מְאוּם בָּרָע וּבָחוֹר בַּטּוֹב, כִּי לֹא בִּבְחִירָתוֹ תַּלְיָא מִלְּתָא, רַק עֶצֶם בְּשָׂרוֹ — בְּשַׂר קֹדֶשׁ. וּלְכָךְ מִיִּצְחָק הוּא הַתְחָלַת תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים עַל דִּיּוּק לְשׁוֹן חֲכָמִים בְּכַמָּה מְקוֹמוֹת: מֹשֶׁה מִפִּי הַגְּבוּרָה, וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר: אוֹרַיְיתָא מִסִּטְרָא דִגְבוּרָה, שֶׁהוּא מַדְרֵגַת יִצְחָק כַּנּוֹדָע; שֶׁהַתּוֹרָה הִיא הַמְיַחֶדֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיִחוּד, שֶׁהֵם קְדוֹשִׁים מֵרֶחֶם. וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ד עַמּוּד א׳): אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּאֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם.
sourceExcerpt.en: The preparation for this was the afflictions of Egypt, which began with Isaac’s birth, as the Sages said. Isaac was the first to be born holy, holy from the womb. Abraham, in contrast, recognized his Creator afterward, and therefore is called “the father of a multitude of nations.” The Sages said at the beginning of Chagigah that he was the first of the converts; in Bikkurim they call Abraham the father of converts. Isaac, however, is the father of Israelites. [Therefore they said in Kiddushin concerning Esau: he was an apostate Israelite.] For this reason Isaac was circumcised at eight days, before he knew anything of evil or of choosing good. The matter does not depend on his choice: his very flesh is holy flesh. Accordingly, Torah begins with Isaac, as I have heard many times concerning the precise expression of the Sages in several places, “Moses, from the mouth of Gevurah.” So too the Zohar says that Torah comes from the side of Gevurah, which is Isaac’s level, as is known. Torah is what especially distinguishes the children of Israel, who are holy from the womb. The Sages said, “Even though he has sinned, he is Israel,” unlike the nations of the world.

h: The Gemara’s teaching and the written and oral Torah

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא שָׁם עַל עָכָן שֶׁעָבַר עַל חֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי,
And this is why they said in the Gemara there concerning Achan that he transgressed all five books of the Torah, etc.,
מוֹשֵׁךְ בְּעָרְלָתוֹ הָיָה וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
and pulled his foreskin, and the like;
וְלָמָּה דָּרְשׁוּ בּוֹ כָּל כָּךְ לִגְנַאי?
yet why did they expound him so disparagingly?
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁבְּעָכָן נִכְתַּב "חָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל",
Rather, because concerning Achan it was written 'Israel has sinned,'
לְהַשְׁמִיעֵנוּ זֶה שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא,
in order to teach us that even though he sinned, he remains Israel,
מִשּׁוּם הָכִי תָּלוּ עָלָיו כָּל מַה שֶּׁיּוּכְלוּ לִתְלוֹת מֵהָרַע,
for this reason they attributed to him every evil they could attribute,
לְלַמֵּד שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
to demonstrate that whatever passes over a Jew,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם "לֹא יִדַּח מִמֶּנּוּ נִדָּח", שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמֶּנּוּ.
nonetheless 'none banished will remain cast away,' for the title of Israel is never uprooted from him.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 38:3: “But the seed of Jacob our father can no longer change their name and uproot themselves from the root of Jewishness. Even if their transgressions grow to the heavens, they are still Israel in every respect. The name Israel is not uprooted from them: it is the holy root in all Jacob’s seed, whose offspring are complete, with no refuse in the root from which all his subsequent seed come. Therefore this root of the name Israel, from Jacob our father, remains forever. Esau, however, although born in holiness, still had the choice to uproot himself from the holiness he had inherited from his fathers.”

h: Holy Shabbos and the written and oral Torah

p: וְזֶה עִנְיַן מַה שֶּׁמָּצִינוּ (שַׁבָּת לג עַמּוּד ב) בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
And this explains what we find (Shabbat 33b) concerning Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and Rabbi Elazar,
כְּשֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִן הַמְּעָרָה: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתְנוּ עֵינֵיהֶם מִיָּד נִשְׂרַף וְכוּלֵי;
when they emerged from the cave: wherever they laid their eyes was instantly consumed by fire, etc.;
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אִיתָא: בַּהֲדָדֵי בְּפַנְיָא דְּמַעֲלֵי שַׁבַּתָּא,
and afterward it is stated: as they walked on Friday afternoon,
חֲזוֹ הַהוּא סָבָא דַּהֲוָה נָקֵיט תְּרֵי מְדָאנֵי אָסָא וְרָהֵיט בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת,
they saw an old man holding two bundles of myrtle, running at twilight;
אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הָנֵי לָמָּה? אֲמַר לְהוּ: לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי, חַד כְּנֶגֶד זָכוֹר וְחַד כְּנֶגֶד שָׁמוֹר;
they asked him: 'What are these for?' He said: 'In honor of Shabbat, one for Zakhor and one for Shamor';
אֲמַר לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ: חֲזִי כַּמָּה חֲבִיבִין מִצְווֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, יְתֵיב דַּעְתַּיְיהוּ.
he said to his son: 'See how beloved the commandments are to Israel!' and their minds were set at ease.
וְצָרִיךְ לְהָבִין מַה שֶּׁנִּתְיַשְּׁבָה דַּעְתָּם בָּזֶה שֶׁרָאוּ בְּהַאי סָבָא שֶׁמְּדַקְדֵּק בְּמִצְווֹת וַחֲבִיבִין עָלָיו,
And one must understand how their minds were calmed merely by observing that this old man was meticulous with mitzvot and held them dear,
וַהֲרֵי עֲדַיִן רָאוּ שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין רוֹב הָעוֹלָם חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְעוֹסְקִין בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה?
when they still witnessed the majority of the world forsaking eternal life to engage in temporal life?
וּבִפְרָט לְפִי מַה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ תּוֹסָפוֹת (חֻלִּין ו עַמּוּד א) בְּשֵׁם יֵשׁ מְפָרְשִׁים,
Especially according to the Tosafot (Chullin 6a) citing in the name of commentators,
דְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁמַּזְכִּיר "הַהוּא סָבָא" הוּא אֵלִיָּהוּ;
that wherever the Talmud mentions 'a certain elder' it refers to Eliyahu;
וְאַף שֶׁכָּתְבוּ הַתּוֹסָפוֹת שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כֵּן בְּשַׁבָּת בְּעוּבְדָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי,
and although Tosafot noted that this cannot be said regarding the end of the narrative in Shabbat,
הַיְינוּ בְּסוֹף הַמַּעֲשֶׂה הַהוּא סָבָא שֶׁאָמַר שֶׁטִּהֵר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי בֵּית הַקְּבָרוֹת דִּמְסַיֵּיק יְהַב בֵּיהּ עֵינֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי,
meaning the elder who mocked Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai for purifying Tiberias upon whom he cast his eyes, etc.,
אֲבָל הַהוּא סָבָא דְּנָקֵט מְדָאנֵי אָסָא יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת אֵלִיָּהוּ.
yet the elder carrying the bundles of myrtles could indeed have been Eliyahu.
אֲבָל יִהְיֶה אֵלִיָּהוּ אוֹ סָבָא אַחֵר, בַּמֶּה נִתְיַשְּׁבָה דַּעְתָּם שֶׁרָאוּ אֶחָד מְחַבֵּב מִצְווֹת,
Yet whether Eliyahu or an ordinary elder, how were they calmed by seeing one individual cherishing mitzvot,
וַהֲרֵי מִקּוֹדֶם אָמַר: מַנִּיחִין חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי?
when previously he protested: 'they forsake eternal life, etc.'?

paragraphs.text: Shabbat 33b:7-8: “They emerged and saw people plowing and sowing. They said: They abandon eternal life and occupy themselves with temporal life. Every place upon which they set their eyes was immediately burned. A heavenly voice went forth and said to them: Have you emerged to destroy My world? Return to your cave! They went back and stayed twelve months. They said: The judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom is twelve months. A heavenly voice went forth and said: Leave your cave! They emerged. Wherever Rabbi Elazar struck, Rabbi Shimon healed. He said to him: My son, you and I suffice for the world. Toward the evening of Sabbath eve, they saw an old man holding two bundles of myrtle and running at twilight. They asked him: Why do you need these? He replied: In honor of the Sabbath. Would one not suffice? One corresponds to “remember,” and one to “guard.” He said to his son: See how dear the commandments are to Israel. Their minds were settled.”

h: The explanation rests on what is taught in the Gemara

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת לה עַמּוּד ב):
Rather, the explanation rests on what is taught in the Gemara (Berakhot 35b):
"וּבִזְמַן שֶׁאֵין יִשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם – מְלַאכְתָּן נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי עַצְמָן,
''And at a time when Israel does not fulfill the will of the Omnipresent, their labor is performed by themselves,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: 'וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ'".
as it is stated: 'And you shall gather your grain.''
וְהִקְשָׁה בְּחִדּוּשֵׁי אַגָּדוֹת רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל אֱלִיעֶזֶר (הַמַּהַרְשָׁ"א):
And Maharsha challenged:
הָא הַפָּרָשָׁה מַיְירֵי: "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ וְגוֹמֵר לְאַהֲבָה אֶת ה' אֱלֹהֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר",
does not the passage state: 'And it shall come to pass if you surely listen... to love Hashem your God, etc.,'
וַעֲלָהּ כְּתִיב "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ",
and upon this it says 'and you shall gather your grain,'!
וְאֵיךְ מוֹקֵי לָהּ בְּאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם?
so how could the Gemara interpret this as not fulfilling the will of the Omnipresent?
וְאָמַרְנוּ, שֶׁלֹּא אָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין מִצְוָתוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, רַק "רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם",
And we explained that the Gemara did not state that they fail to perform His commandments, but rather His 'will';
וְהַיְינוּ דְּוַדַּאי לֹא צִוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לִשְׁבּוֹת כָּל הַיָּמִים,
meaning that Hashem certainly did not command man to cease labor every day,
רַק לִשְׁבּוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת וּשְׁמִיטָה, וְזֶה שׁוֹמְרִין יִשְׂרָאֵל.
commanding rest only on Shabbat and Shemittah, which Israel fully observes.
רַק רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אָמַר, כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדוּעַ שֶׁרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הָאָדָם פָּנוּי רַק לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
Only Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai maintained that since it is known that the divine ideal will is for man to be dedicated exclusively to Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָאָדָם שׁוּם עֵסֶק בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
just as it was prior to Adam's sin when man had no preoccupation with worldly affairs,
וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם.
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai asserted that a Jew ought to realize this transcendent will of the Omnipresent.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין צט עַמּוּד ב):
And as written (Sanhedrin 99b):
"כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: 'לֹא יָמוּשׁ וְגוֹמֵר' – הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה נִבְרָא וְכוּלֵי,
''When it says 'shall not depart, etc.'—say that he was created for the toil of Torah, etc.,
טוּבֵיהּ לִדְזָכֵי דַּהֲוֵי דְּרוֹפְתְּקֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא",
happy is he who merits to become the pack-bearer (wholly consumed) of Torah,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁצָּרִיךְ לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה דְּרוֹפְתְּקֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְיוּחָד רַק לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה,
meaning one must merit to be totally dedicated solely to the toil of Torah,
וְזֶה נִקְרָא "עוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם" וּמְלַאכְתּוֹ נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים.
and this is called fulfilling the will of the Omnipresent wherein his labor is done by others.

footnotes.enAnchorPrefix: Rather, the explanation rests on what is taught in the Gemara (Berakhot 35b):

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 35b:7: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says: Is it possible that a person plows in the plowing season and sows in the sowing season and harvests in the harvest season and threshes in the threshing season and winnows in the windy season, as grain is separated from the chaff by means of the wind, and is constantly busy; what will become of Torah? Rather, one must dedicate himself exclusively to Torah at the expense of other endeavors; as when Israel performs God’s will, their work is performed by others, as it is stated: “And strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and your vinedressers” (Isaiah 61:5). When Israel does not perform God’s will, their work is performed by them themselves, as it is stated: “And you shall gather your grain.” Moreover, if Israel fails to perform God’s will, others’ work will be performed by them, as it is stated: “You shall serve your enemy whom God shall send against you, in hunger, in thirst, in nakedness and in want of all things” (Deuteronomy 28:48).”

paragraphs.text: Chidushei Agadot on Berakhot 35b:2 (Maharsha): ““As it is said, You shall gather your grain,” and so forth: This requires examination. How can the verse “You shall gather your grain” be applied to those who do not perform the will of the Omnipresent? It explicitly says, “If you surely listen,” and “to love the Lord,” and in that context it says, “I will give rain,” and “you shall gather your grain.” Conversely, concerning those who do not perform the will of the Omnipresent it says, “Beware lest,” and “there will be no rain.””

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 99b:2: “Rabbi Elazar says: Every man was created for labor, as it is stated: “Man is born for toil” (Job 5:7). Based on this verse, I do not know whether he was created for toil of the mouth, speech, or whether he was created for the toil of labor. When the verse states: “For his mouth presses upon him” (Proverbs 16:26), you must say that he was created for toil of the mouth. And still I do not know with regard to the toil of the mouth whether it is for the toil of Torah or for the toil of conversation. When the verse states: “This Torah scroll shall not depart from your mouth” (Joshua 1:8), you must say that he was created for the toil of Torah. And that is the meaning of what Rava said: All bodies are like receptacles to store items until use. Happy is one who is privileged, who is a receptacle for Torah.”

p: אֲבָל צָרִיךְ לִזְכּוֹת לָזֶה כְּמוֹ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא,
However, one must uniquely merit this, like Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa,
דְּאִיתָא (תַּעֲנִית כד עַמּוּד ב): "וַחֲנִינָא בְּנִי דַּיּוֹ בְּקַב חֲרוּבִין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת",
of whom it is taught (Ta'anit 24b): 'And My son Chanina is satisfied with a kav of carobs from one Sabbath eve to the next,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכָּל יְמֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ הָיָה מִתְעַנֶּה, וְלִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת הָיָה אוֹכֵל הַחֲרוּבִין,
meaning that all weekdays he fasted, eating carobs only for the honor of Shabbat,
וְנִרְאֶה שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה הֶפְקֵר לַכֹּל.
and it appears these carobs were ownerless for all.
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מֵהָא דְּאִיתָא הָתָם:
And so it appears from what is brought there:
דַּהֲוָה רְגִילָה דְּבֵיתְהוּ לְמֵיחְמָא תַּנּוּרָא כָּל מַעֲלֵי דְּשַׁבַּתָּא וְכוּלֵי,
that his wife was accustomed to heating the oven every Sabbath eve, etc.,
וּמַשְׁמָע שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם שׁוּם דָּבָר עַל שַׁבָּת רַק הַקַּב חֲרוּבִין;
implying they had nothing for Shabbat except the kav of carobs;
וּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב "מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת",
and that which is stated 'from Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve'
הַכַּוָּנָה מִשַּׁבָּת לְשַׁבָּת לְצוֹרֶךְ שַׁבָּת,
means from one Sabbath to the next for the necessity of Shabbat,
וּכְעֵין שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (חֻלִּין פד עַמּוּד א): "וְאִינָךְ אֵימַת? מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת",
similar to what we find (Chullin 84a): 'And when for the rest? From Sabbath eve to Sabbath eve,'
שֶׁבְּוַדַּאי הַמְּכֻוָּון שָׁם שֶׁהַבָּשָׂר וְכַדּוֹמֶה אָכְלוּ בְּשַׁבָּת.
where it certainly means that meat and the like were eaten on Shabbat.
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ (עֵירוּבִין כב עַמּוּד א) בְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא
And so we find (Eruvin 22a) regarding Rav Adda bar Mattana,
שֶׁאָמַר: "מִי שְׁלִימוּ קוּרְמֵי בְּאַגְמָא",
who said: 'Have the reeds in the marsh ended?!'
וְרָבָא דָּרַשׁ: "'שְׁחֹרוֹת כָּעוֹרֵב' – בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ אַכְזָרִי עַל בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵּיתוֹ כְּעוֹרֵב".
and Rava expounded: ''Black as a raven'—in one who makes himself ruthless toward his children and household like a raven.'
אֲבָל הֵם לֹא נִטְרְדוּ כְּלָל מִזֶּה,
Yet they were not disturbed by this at all,
וְעָרַב לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא לְהִתְעַנּוֹת מִשַּׁבָּת לְשַׁבָּת וְגִלְגֵּל עַצְמוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת בְּקַב חֲרוּבִין,
and it was pleasing for Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa to fast from Sabbath to Sabbath and survive on a kav of carobs on Shabbat,
וְכֵן לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָא לְהִתְאַכְזֵר עַל בְּנֵי בֵּיתוֹ כְּעוֹרֵב כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ פְּנוּיִם לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה.
and likewise for Rav Adda bar Mattana to appear ruthless toward his household like a raven so as to remain unburdened for the toil of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 7:1: “Because of this closeness that he had, he also had the power to restrain himself concerning all the good things in the world, so that they would flow to Israel in greater abundance, although in truth all those good things descended only through him. Thus the Talmud says: “The whole world is sustained through Chanina My son, and Chanina My son is satisfied with a kav of carobs from one Shabbat ….” This was because he was very close to God and saw clearly, as it truly is, “The Lord our God, the Lord is one.” Therefore his generosity was so immense. Indeed, every individual soul that has great generosity toward its community can also bring about all their deliverances, even above nature. To indicate this, the Talmud brings all the wondrous events concerning Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Divrei Soferim 30:1: “But a kav sufficed for him, for God “satisfies the desire of every living thing,” according to its desire. King Solomon asked, “Provide me with my allotted bread,” according to his own need for bread, in Solomon’s meal in its time. This counted for him as his allotted bread according to his need for sustenance, and not as excess, for he asked, “Give me neither poverty nor wealth”: neither less than his need nor excess. For Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa, a kav of carobs counted as his allotted bread. More than that would have been excess and wealth, concerning which he should ask, “Do not give me”; his poverty would have been less even than a kav of carobs. The entire world was sustained through him, each with his allotted bread: whoever needs a meal like Solomon’s, a horse to ride, and a servant to run before him—all his requirements are included in the sustenance drawn to each person through him.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: רַק שֶׁהוּא דַּי לוֹ בְּקַב, כִּי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ "מַשְׂבִּיעַ לְכָל חַי רָצוֹן" כְּפִי רְצוֹנוֹ, וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם בִּקֵּשׁ "הַטְרִיפֵנִי לֶחֶם חֻקִּי" כְּפִי צֹרֶךְ הַלֶּחֶם שֶׁלּוֹ בִּסְעֻדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה בִּשְׁעָתָהּ, וְזֶה נֶחְשָׁב אֶצְלוֹ לְלֶחֶם חֻקִּי כְּפִי צֹרֶךְ פַּרְנָסָתוֹ, וְלֹא מוֹתָרוֹת, דְּבִקֵּשׁ עַל זֶה: "רֵישׁ וָעֹשֶׁר אַל תִּתֶּן לִי", לֹא שֶׁיֶּחְסַר לוֹ מִכְּדֵי צָרְכּוֹ וְלֹא מוֹתָרוֹת; וְאֵצֶל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא נֶחְשָׁב קַב חֲרוּבִין לֶחֶם חֻקִּי, וְיוֹתֵר מִזֶּה הָיָה אֶצְלוֹ מוֹתָרוֹת וְעֹשֶׁר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לְבַקֵּשׁ עַל זֶה שֶׁ"אַל תִּתֶּן לִי", וְרֵישׁוּתוֹ הָיָה פָּחוֹת גַּם מִקַּב חֲרוּבִין, וְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ נִזּוֹן בִּשְׁבִילוֹ כָּל אֶחָד בְּלֶחֶם חֻקּוֹ, מִי שֶׁצָּרִיךְ כִּסְעֻדַּת שְׁלֹמֹה וְסוּס לִרְכֹּב וְעֶבֶד לָרוּץ לְפָנָיו, כָּל הִצְטָרְכוּתוֹ הוּא בִּכְלַל מְזוֹנֵי הַנִּמְשָׁךְ לְכָל אֶחָד בִּשְׁבִילוֹ.

h: One who cannot endure such a trial— behold, Rava himself said

p: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לַעֲמוֹד בְּנִסָּיוֹן זֶה,
However, one who cannot endure such a trial—
הָא רָבָא בְּעַצְמוֹ אָמַר (בְּרָכוֹת שָׁם):
behold, Rava himself said (Berakhot there):
"בְּיוֹמֵי נִיסָן וּבְיוֹמֵי תִּשְׁרֵי לָא תִּתְחֲזוּ קַמַּאי וְכוּלֵי",
''In the days of Nisan and Tishrei do not appear before me, etc.,''
הֲרֵי שֶׁאַף שֶׁהָיוּ אָמוֹרָאִים וְרַבָּנָן תַּלְמִידָיו,
so even though they were Amoraim and scholarly disciples,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּדַע שֶׁהֶעְדֵּר הַמְּזוֹנוֹת יַטְרִיד לָהֶם,
since he knew that a lack of sustenance would agitate them,
צִוָּה שֶׁיַּעַסְקוּ בְּפַרְנָסָתָם בִּימֵי נִיסָן וְתִשְׁרֵי.
he instructed that they attend to their livelihood in the harvest months of Nisan and Tishrei.
וְעַל זֶה מַיְירֵי הַפָּרָשָׁה: "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶל מִצְוֺתַי וְגוֹמֵר וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ וְגוֹמֵר",
And concerning this the passage speaks: 'And it shall come to pass if you surely listen to My commandments, etc., and you shall gather your grain, etc.,'
דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁעוֹשִׂין מִצְוֹת ה' שֶׁצִּוָּה לִשְׁבּוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת וּשְׁמִיטָה,
namely that they observe the commandments of Hashem Who commanded to rest on Shabbat and Shemittah,
אֲבָל אֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם לִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי רַק לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה,
yet do not attain the ultimate will of the Omnipresent to remain free solely for the toil of Torah,
וְזֶהוּ "מְלַאכְתָּן נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי עַצְמָן".
and this is why 'their labor is done by themselves.'
אֲבָל מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִהְיוֹת דְּרוֹפְתְּקֵי דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא לִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי רַק לַעֲמַל תּוֹרָה כִּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
However, one who merits to become the pack-bearer of Torah, dedicated solely to its toil according to the supernal will,
מְלַאכְתּוֹ נַעֲשֵׂית עַל יְדֵי אֲחֵרִים,
his labor is done by others;
וְלָאו כָּל אָדָם זוֹכֶה לָזֶה.
yet not every person merits this.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם: "הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ וְכוּלֵי כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי וְלֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדָן".
And this is what they said there: 'Many acted like Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and it did not succeed in their hand.'

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: וְכֵן הַבִּיאָה לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַיְנוּ לְהִשְׁתַּדֵּל בְּצָרְכֵי הַגּוּף וְלִנְהֹג בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרֵישׁ פֶּרֶק כֵּיצַד מְבָרְכִין (בְּרָכוֹת דַּף ל״ה עַמּוּד ב׳). "וְלֹא נִתְּנָה תוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי הַמָּן" (מְכִילְתָּא פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח) — הַיְנוּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי שָׁם דִּדְבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן [סוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב — מִדַּת יוֹם, אֲבָל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הִיא מִדַּת לַיְלָה, דַּרְגָּא דְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כַּנּוֹדָע]. וּמָן הוּא לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים (יוֹמָא דַּף ע״ה עַמּוּד ב׳), הַיְנוּ בְּלֹא שׁוּם הֲנָאָה לַגּוּף רַק לַנֶּפֶשׁ. וְלָכֵן לֹא הָיָה מִמֶּנּוּ פְּסֹלֶת כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שָׁם, כִּי הָיָה כֻּלּוֹ לַהשֵּׁם. וְהַפְּסֹלֶת הוּא מִמַּה שֶּׁנִּתְכַּוֵּן לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ [דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר בְּזוּלַת זֶה גַּם בַּאֲכִילָה, שֶׁשְּׁנֵיהֶם נִקְרָאִים בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲכִילָה: "אָכְלָה וּמָחֲתָה פִיהָ", וְכַנּוֹדָע בְּסוֹד חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן בַּאֲכִילָה, וְהוּא מֻשְׁרָשׁ בְּכָל הַדּוֹרוֹת כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן לְגַמְרֵי עַד מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד]. וְלֹא יָרַד רַק "עַד בֹּאָם אֶל קְצֵה אֶרֶץ כְּנָעַן" (שְׁמוֹת ט״ז, ל״ה), כִּידוּעַ בְּסוֹד הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וּשְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם. וְהַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא שֶׁפַע כָּל מִינֵי חֶמְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה. וְכֵן אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל נִשְׁתַּבְּחָה בְּכָל מִינֵי חֲמָדוֹת, רַק שֶׁהִיא אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהִיא אֶרֶץ הַקְּדוֹשָׁה שֶׁכָּל מִינֵי חֲמָדוֹת שֶׁלָּהּ הַכֹּל בִּקְדֻשָּׁה וְהַכָּרָה שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְצָרִיךְ מִקּוֹדֶם שֶׁיִּבָּלְעוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בְּתוֹכָן בְּאוֹתָן אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מְכִילְתָּא שָׁם).

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Tzidkat HaTzadik 224:1: “Everyone must also recite the first paragraph [of the Shema]: at the beginning of his daily acceptance of the kingdom of Heaven, he must be disposed in this way, even to surrender everything if this should be God’s will. A person who conducts himself according to the ordinary way of the world and within bounds does so because “many acted … and did not succeed”: this is not God’s will [for them]. Even those exceptional individuals must also recite “If you indeed listen,” just as Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai was told to return to the cave. paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 70:2: “Concerning Samuel the prophet, we find that Hannah prayed, “Give Your maidservant offspring among men.” The Sages explained: offspring unobtrusive among men, neither tall nor short, neither wise nor foolish, and so forth. That is, she prayed that he should have composure, for in this world God chose service carried out with a settled mind, rather than a person constantly nullifying his body and soul altogether. Thus, when the Holy One told Samuel to go to David and anoint him king, Samuel answered, “How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me ….” This answer, given with composure, found great favor in God’s eyes; the proof is that God gave him counsel in response. With Jonah son of Amittai, however, when the prophet sent him to anoint Jehu, he immediately risked his life. Although the danger was greater than Samuel’s, he paid no attention to his life by asking how he could go to such a dangerous place. Yet at the rejoicing of the water drawing, when Israel stand in great love and generosity of heart toward one another, God likewise illuminates the immense generosity of His love for Israel. Jonah son of Amittai was therefore chosen then to be a prophet over Israel, although his love involved an excessive self-effacement beyond the bounds of this world’s order. As the Mekhilta states, “Jonah demanded the honor of the son and did not demand the honor of the father”: love of Israel was so firmly planted in his heart that he always demanded the son’s honor, rather than the father’s.”

Saul will hear and kill me ….” This answer, given with composure, found great favor in God’s eyes; the proof is that God gave him counsel in response. With Jonah son of Amittai, however, when the prophet sent him to anoint Jehu, he immediately risked his life. Although the danger was greater than Samuel’s, he paid no attention to his life by asking how he could go to such a dangerous place. Yet at the rejoicing of the water drawing, when Israel stand in great love and generosity of heart toward one another, God likewise illuminates the immense generosity of His love for Israel. Jonah son of Amittai was therefore chosen then to be a prophet over Israel, although his love involved an excessive self-effacement beyond the bounds of this world’s order. As the Mekhilta states, “Jonah demanded the honor of the son and did not demand the honor of the father”: love of Israel was so firmly planted in his heart that he always demanded the son’s honor, rather than the father’s.

h: Holy Shabbos and the written and oral Torah — the holiness of Israel

p: וְזֶה שֶׁהֶרְאָה לָהֶם הַאי סָבָא עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ: "מַנִּיחִין חַיֵּי עוֹלָם וְעוֹסְקִין בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה",
And this is what that elder showed them regarding their protest: 'they forsake eternal life and engage in temporal life':
שֶׁלִּכְבוֹד הַשַּׁבָּת נָקֵיט מְדָאנֵי אָסָא לְעַנֵּג הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁנִּצְטַוּוּ לְעַנְּגוֹ;
that for the honor of Shabbat he took bundles of myrtle to delight the Sabbath which they were commanded to delight;
וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: "חֲזִי כַּמָּה חֲבִיבִין מִצְווֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל",
and Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said: 'See how beloved the commandments are to Israel!'
הַיְינוּ הַמִּצְוָה שֶׁצִּוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָנוּחַ בְּשַׁבָּת וְלִהְיוֹת פָּנוּי רַק לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
namely the commandment that Hashem commanded to rest on Shabbat and be free solely for His service,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּבְרָא הָאָדָם רַק לְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת קוֹנוֹ,
just as man was created only to serve his Master,
מְדַקְדְּקִין יִשְׂרָאֵל וְחָבִיב עֲלֵיהֶם לְהוֹסִיף עֹנֶג לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת.
Israel is meticulous and eager to add delight for the honor of Shabbat.
וְאִם הָיָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְצַוֶּוה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לִשְׁבּוֹת כָּל הַיָּמִים, הָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִין גַּם כֵּן,
And had Hashem commanded Israel to rest all days, they would likewise obey,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁשּׁוֹבְתִין בִּשְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִיטָה שֶׁצִּוָּה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לָנוּחַ מִכָּל עֲבוֹדָה;
just as they rest in the Shemittah year wherein Hashem commanded cessation from all agricultural work;
וּמִזֶּה יְתֵיב דַּעְתַּיְיהוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁעוֹסְקִין בְּחַיֵּי שָׁעָה,
and from this their minds were calmed regarding the people's engagement in worldly life,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּיתַּן רְשׁוּת לַעֲבוֹד בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה.
since permission was formally granted to work during the six days of action.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 11:10: “This was Abraham our father’s attribute: he did not wish to extend himself in the affairs of this world like the people of his generation. Even in the matters of holiness God granted him, he did not extend himself, for his heart was firm and confident in God: with God there is holiness greater and broader than the sea, greater than the measure of human apprehension—life of life without end or limit, a holiness beyond even his power to anticipate and hope for. The Holy One appeared to him and said, “I am the owner of the palace”: to you and to the generations who follow your footsteps I shall show that I govern all the world’s affairs. Even in this world’s affairs they will find words of the living God. Since, on your part, you do not choose what would distract you with temporary life, My will is alive for you in all the affairs of the world.”

h: Bundles of myrtle for the groom and the bride

p: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמַר: "וּמְדָאנֵי אָסָא לַאֲרוּס וַאֲרוּסָה",
And this explains the verse: 'and bundles of myrtle for the groom and the bride':
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא: "חַד כְּנֶגֶד זָכוֹר וְחַד כְּנֶגֶד שָׁמוֹר",
for it aligns with what is taught in the Gemara: 'one for Zakhor and one for Shamor,'
וּבָרַמְבַּ"ן יִתְרוֹ כָּתַב בְּשֵׁם סֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר,
and the Ramban in Yitro wrote in the name of Sefer HaBahir,
דְּ"שָׁמוֹר" הִיא שַׁבָּת מַלְכְּתָא, וְ"זָכוֹר" כְּנֶגֶד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
that 'Shamor' is the Sabbath Queen, and 'Zakhor' corresponds to Hashem, blessed be He,
וְזֶהוּ "לַאֲרוּס וַאֲרוּסָה".
and this is 'for the groom and bride.'
וְאָמַר: "לְאִתְקָפָא חַלָּשִׁין",
And he stated: 'to strengthen the weak,'
וְהַיְינוּ הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי שֶׁהוּא חָלוּשׁ בְּדַעְתּוֹ עַל מַה שֶּׁטָּרוּד בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
meaning the Jew whose spirit is faint over being preoccupied during weekdays with worldly pursuits.
וְאָמַר מִקּוֹדֶם "לַאֲרוּס וַאֲרוּסָה", עַד דֻּגְמַת מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים",
And he mentioned first 'for the groom and bride,' reflecting that which is written: 'Ascribe strength unto God,'
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁעוֹשִׂין לִכְבוֹד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יָהֲבִין תּוּקְפָא וְחֵילָא כִּבְיָכוֹל לְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
for through what they do for the honor of Hashem they grant strength and power, as it were, to the Holy One,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, לב סוֹף עַמּוּד ב),
as written in the holy Zohar (Part II, 32b end),
וְזֶהוּ "לְאִתְקָפָא חַלָּשִׁין".
and this is 'to strengthen the weak.'

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 182: “What is the meaning of “remember” and “guard”? “Remember” pertains to the male, and “guard” to the bride. What is the meaning of “revere My sanctuary”? Guard yourselves against improper thought, for My sanctuary is holy. Why? “For I am the Lord who sanctifies you” in everything.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bo 2:7 (II 32b): “When Israel’s deeds are not proper, those appointed messengers, when they seek to stand against Israel’s deeds, stand, as it were, against the Lord Himself. For when Israel performs improper deeds, they weaken, as it were, the power of the Holy One, blessed be He. When they perform proper deeds, they give strength and power to the Holy One, blessed be He. Therefore it is written, “Give strength to God.” Through what? Through proper deeds. Therefore, on that day, all the appointed rulers gathered against the Lord—against the Lord Himself, for since they gathered against Israel, they gathered against Him.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Kometz HaMinchah 1:6:1: ““If you are righteous, what do you give Him?” As Midrash Tanchuma says: What difference does it make to the Holy One whether one slaughters from the neck …? Therefore, “The reward of a commandment is a commandment.” Elsewhere, however, they said, “Give strength to God”; and when, God forbid, someone sins, he weakens the strength of the heavenly retinue. It is then like one who hires someone to work on his own property and pays his full wage. Both are true: the first concerns His essence, and the second the extension of His attributes, which the Sages call the Shekhinah. Thus the Talmud says: When a person sins, what does the Shekhinah say? “My head is heavy ….” This is “They enjoy the radiance of the Shekhinah.””

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: וְ"אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ" [אִיּוֹב ל״ה:ז׳], כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא (שְׁמִינִי [סִימָן ח׳]): מָה אִכְפַּת לֵיהּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בֵּין שׁוֹחֵט מִן הַצַּוָּאר וְכוּלֵי, לָכֵן "שְׂכַר מִצְוָה — מִצְוָה". אֲבָל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר אָמְרוּ: "תְּנוּ עֹז לֵאלֹהִים" [תְּהִלִּים ס״ח:ל״ה], וּכְשֶׁחַס וְשָׁלוֹם חוֹטֵא — מַתִּישׁ כֹּחַ פַּמַּלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה; וְאִם כֵּן דִּינוֹ כְּשׂוֹכֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת בְּשֶׁלּוֹ, דְּנוֹתֵן שְׂכָרוֹ מִשָּׁלֵם. וּשְׁנֵיהֶם אֱמֶת: הָרִאשׁוֹן — בְּעַצְמוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ; וְהַשֵּׁנִי — בְּהִתְפַּשְּׁטוּת מִדּוֹתָיו, וְהוּא הַנִּקְרָא בְּרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה "שְׁכִינָה", כְּמַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סַנְהֶדְרִין מ״ו עַמּוּד א׳): כְּשֶׁאָדָם חוֹטֵא, שְׁכִינָה מָה אוֹמֶרֶת? "קַלַּנִי מֵרֹאשִׁי וְכוּלֵי". וְזֶהוּ: "וְנֶהֱנִין מִזִּיו הַשְּׁכִינָה" [בְּרָכוֹת י״ז עַמּוּד א׳]:

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 25:3: “Concerning this it says, “Sound the shofar at the new moon …,” in the manner of “Give strength to God,” as explained in the holy Zohar: “They give strength and power to the Holy One ….” On Rosh Hashanah renewal is awakened again. This is only from the side of creation, for from His side no renewal applies, since nothing grows old from His side. Thus the Talmud says that the prince of the world said the verse, “I was young, and have also grown old”: could one say it was the Holy One—does old age apply to Him? The prince of the world is the point God placed in all creation, that it should recognize it has no power of its own. Concerning that point the Sages said, “There is no blade of grass below that has no mazal above ….” This recognition is, in truth, creation’s essential strength, as stated in the holy Zohar.”

h: Wine and spiritual joy and the written and oral Torah

p: וְצֵירֵף לָזֶה הַיַּיִן קִדּוּשׁ, שֶׁגַּם הוּא בָּא לְאִתְקָפָא חַלָּשִׁין,
And he joined to this the wine of Kiddush, which likewise comes to strengthen the weak,
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (עֵירוּבִין סה עַמּוּד א):
and this is based upon what is stated (Eruvin 65a):
"לֹא נִבְרָא יַיִן אֶלָּא לְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים וּלְשַׁלֵּם שָׂכָר לָרְשָׁעִים וְכוּלֵי";
''Wine was created only to comfort mourners and to pay reward to the wicked, etc.'';
וְקָשֶׁה, הָא יֵשׁ יַיִן דְּמִצְוָה,
and it is difficult: behold, there is wine of mitzvah,
וּלְפֵירוּשׁ רַשִּׁ"י (נָזִיר ד עַמּוּד א) קִדּוּשׁ עַל הַיַּיִן דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא וּמִקְרֵי מוּשְׁבָּע וְעוֹמֵד,
and according to Rashi (Nazir 4a) Kiddush over wine is biblical such that one is considered foresworn from Sinai,
וְאַף לַתּוֹסָפוֹת שֶׁכָּתְבוּ שֶׁהוּא מִדְּרַבָּנָן עַל כָּל פָּנִים יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִצְוָה;
and even according to Tosafot who hold it is rabbinic, it is at any rate a mitzvah;
וּלְבַד זֶה אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת מב עַמּוּד ב): "בְּשַׁבָּתוֹת וְיוֹם טוֹב וְכוּלֵי הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם קוֹבֵעַ סְעוּדָתוֹ עַל הַיַּיִן".
and besides this they taught (Berakhot 42b): 'On Sabbaths and festivals, etc., since a person establishes his meal upon wine.'
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ יַיִן לְטוֹבָה,
And so we find wine praised positively,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (יוֹמָא עו עַמּוּד ב): "זָכָה נַעֲשָׂה רֹאשׁ וְכוּלֵי, זָכָה מְשַׂמְּחוֹ וְכוּלֵי, חַמְרָא וְרֵיחָנֵי פִּקְחִין".
as written (Yoma 76b): 'If he merits he becomes a head, if he merits it gladdens him, wine and fragrance enlighten.'
וְכֵן מָצִינוּ (עֵירוּבִין סד עַמּוּד א) דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
And so we find (Eruvin 64a) that Rav Nachman said:
"כָּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא שָׁתֵינָא רְבִיעֲתָא דְּחַמְרָא – לָא צִילָאי דַּעְתַּאי".
''As long as I have not drunk a revi'it of wine, my mind is not clear.''
וּבְאוֹתָהּ סוּגְיָא בְּעֵירוּבִין גַּם כֵּן אִיתָא:
And in that same passage in Eruvin it is likewise taught:
"כָּל הַמִּתְפַּתֶּה בְּיֵינוֹ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִדַּעַת קוֹנוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
''Whoever is appeased through his wine has within him of the disposition of his Creator, etc.,
כָּל הַמִּתְיַשֵּׁב בְּיֵינוֹ יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּעַת שִׁבְעִים זְקֵנִים וְכוּלֵי",
whoever remains settled in his wine possesses the wisdom of seventy elders, etc.,''
וּמָצִינוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין לח עַמּוּד א): "אַגְבָּרוּ חַמְרָא אַדַּרְדְּקֵי כִּי הֵיכֵי דְּלֵימְרוּ מִלְּתָא".
and we find (Sanhedrin 38a): 'Give wine to the youths so they may state a novel thought.'
וְגַם בַּתּוֹרָה מָצִינוּ מְפוֹרָשׁ יַיִן נְסָכִים לַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
And also in the Torah we find explicit libation wine for the Altar,
וְאֵיךְ אָמַר שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא הַיַּיִן רַק לְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים?
so how could the Gemara state that wine was created only to comfort mourners?

h: The Midrash: the matter is based on what is stated : 'I have

p: אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "דְּרָכָיו רָאִיתִי וְאֶרְפָּאֵהוּ, וְאַשְׁלֵם נִחוּמִים לוֹ וְלַאֲבֵלָיו",
Rather, the matter is based on what is stated (Isaiah 57:18): 'I have seen his ways and will heal him; I will lead him also, and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners,'
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה טז): "אֵלּוּ אֵבָרָיו הַמִּתְאַבְּלִין עָלָיו";
and in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 16 end): 'These are his limbs that mourn over him';
וּבְרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (חֵלֶק ג, קכג עַמּוּד א) אַחַר שֶׁהֶאֱרִיךְ בְּעִנְיַן הַתְּשׁוּבָה, אִיתָא:
and in Ra'aya Meheimna (Part III, 123a), after elaborating on repentance, it states:
"וְכָל פִּקּוּדִין דַּעֲשֵׂה דַּהֲווֹ עֲתִידִין לְשַׁרְיָא בִּרְמַ"ח אֵבָרִין דִּילֵיהּ כֻּלְּהוּ מִתְאַבְּלִין עֲלֵיהּ,
''And all positive commandments that were destined to rest upon his 248 limbs all mourn over him,
וְרָזָא דְּמִלָּה 'דְּרָכָיו רָאִיתִי וְגוֹמֵר וְלַאֲבֵלָיו' – אִלֵּין רְמַ"ח אֵיבָרִין דְּקָא מִתְאַבְּלָן עֲלֵיהּ וְכוּלֵי".
and the secret of the matter is 'I have seen his ways, etc., and to his mourners'—these are the 248 limbs that mourn over him, etc.''
וְזֶה כַּוָּנַת הַגְּמָרָא "לֹא נִבְרָא יַיִן אֶלָּא לְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים",
And this is the meaning of the Gemara 'Wine was created only to comfort mourners,'
שֶׁאַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל נִבְרָא הַיַּיִן לְשַׂמֵּחַ הַלֵּב;
for following Adam's sin, wine was created to gladden the heart;
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (תַּעֲנִית טו עַמּוּד א): "'יְשָׁרִים לְשִׂמְחָה' – לִישְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה",
and it is based on what is stated (Ta'anit 15a): ''The upright are for gladness'—gladness is for the upright of heart,'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב זוֹכִין לְשִׂמְחָה,
meaning when one merits to straighten the heart he merits joy,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא: "זָכָה מְשַׂמְּחוֹ", דִּכְתִיב: "וְיַיִן יְשַׂמַּח לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ".
and this is what they taught: 'if he merits it gladdens him,' as written: 'and wine gladdens the heart of man.'

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Machshavot Charutz 19:4: “This is what Adam was warned about, for “God made the human being upright.” The whole world is one complete body. When the body is complete, there is no need to work to bring love of other creatures into the heart: it is natural, just as a person loves the limbs of his body. “Wine was created only to console mourners …” means that, because there are pain and trouble in the world, one needs to seek joy—“Let him drink and forget his poverty.” But someone who is already joyful should not seek added joy in this world while the Holy One has not rejoiced in His world with complete joy through Adam’s fulfillment of his commandment: not to seek and desire added joy that God does not give him.”

h: Holy Shabbos and the written and oral Torah — the Zohar’s teaching

p: וְהַפָּסוּק "דְּרָכָיו רָאִיתִי וְגוֹמֵר" מַיְירֵי לֶעָתִיד,
And the verse 'I have seen his ways, etc.' speaks of the future,
דִּלְעֵיל מִנֵּיהּ כְּתִיב: "כִּי לֹא לְעוֹלָם אָרִיב וְגוֹמֵר כִּי רוּחַ מִלְּפָנַי יַעֲטוֹף וְגוֹמֵר",
for prior to it is written: 'For I will not contend forever, etc., for the spirit should fail before Me, etc.,'
וּמִנֵּיהּ דָּרְשׁוּ (יְבָמוֹת סב עַמּוּד א): "אֵין בֶּן דָּוִד בָּא עַד שֶׁיִּכְלוּ כָּל הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁבַּגּוּף",
from which they expounded (Yevamot 62a): 'The Son of David does not come until all souls in the Guf are depleted,'
וְאַחַר כָּךְ כְּתִיב: "דְּרָכָיו רָאִיתִי וְאֶרְפָּאֵהוּ וְאַנְחֵהוּ",
and afterward it is written: 'I have seen his ways and will heal him; I will lead him,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיַּכְנִיס בּוֹ נִיחָא כְּעֵין מְנוּחַת שַׁבָּת,
meaning He will infuse within him serenity akin to the rest of Shabbat,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה טז): "'וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ' – נָתַן לוֹ מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת, כְּדִבּוּרוֹ 'וַיָּנַח בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי'",
and as they expounded (Bereishit Rabbah 16): ''And He placed him'—He gave him the commandment of Shabbat, matching 'and He rested on the seventh day,''
וְהַיְינוּ דְּשָׁם גַּם כֵּן הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהָיָה לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִיחָא בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי.
meaning there too the explanation is that Hashem had delight on the seventh day.
וְשַׁבָּת הוּא "מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת נז עַמּוּד ב),
And Shabbat is 'a semblance of the World to Come,' as written (Berakhot 57b),
וְכֵן נִדְרָשׁ (בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק א, מח עַמּוּד ב): "'בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה' לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ' – עַל יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת",
and so it is expounded (Zohar I 48b): ''In the day that Hashem shall give you rest from your sorrow and from your trouble'—upon the Sabbath day,'
שֶׁאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נוֹתֵן נִיחָא בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל מַה שֶּׁהוּא עָצֵב מִמַּה שֶּׁהָיָה מְשׁוּקָּע בִּימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּעִנְיְנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
for then Hashem infuses serenity into the heart of Israel over their sadness from being immersed during weekdays in worldly pursuits,
וּמֵהָרוֹגֶז וּמֵהַחֲרָדָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מִמִּלְחֶמֶת הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
and from the anxiety and fear arising from the battle against the evil inclination.
וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וַאֲשַׁלֵּם נִחֻמִים לוֹ וְלַאֲבֵלָיו" – אֵלּוּ רְמַ"ח אֵבָרִים הַמִּתְאַבְּלִים עָלָיו.
And concerning this Scripture proclaims: 'and restore comforts unto him and to his mourners'—these are the 248 limbs mourning over him.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא שָׁם לְעֵיל מִנֵּיהּ,
And as written in Ra'aya Meheimna there above,
דְּעַל הַאי דִּיוּקְנָא דְּאוֹת הֵ"א אוֹקְמוּהָ: "מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי בְּבֵית גְּנָזַי וְשַׁבָּת שְׁמָהּ וְכוּלֵי",
that upon this image of the letter Hei they established: 'I have a precious gift in My treasury and Shabbat is its name, etc.,'
וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר: "וְכַד הִיא תֵּיזִיל מִנֵּיהּ הוּא סַם הַמָּוֶת וְכוּלֵי, וּבְהַהוּא זִמְנָא אִתְקְרֵי בַּר נָשׁ מֵת וְכוּלֵי",
and afterward it states: 'and when it departs from him it is the potion of death, etc., and at that moment man is termed dead, etc.,'
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל תִּקְּנוּ קִדּוּשׁ עַל הַיַּיִן לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב וּלְשַׂמְּחוֹ,
and therefore following the fall they instituted Kiddush over wine to straighten the heart and gladden it,
וְהוּא לְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים כָּאָמוּר;
which serves to comfort mourners as explained;
אֲבָל קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל לֹא נִצְרַךְ כְּלָל הַיַּיִן.
whereas prior to the fall, wine was not required at all.

paragraphs.text: Yevamot 62a:17: “The Gemara clarifies the reasons for their opinions: Rav Huna said he has fulfilled the mitzva due to a statement of Rav Asi, as Rav Asi said that the reason for this mitzva is that the Messiah, son of David, will not come until all the souls of the body have been finished, i.e., until all souls that are destined to inhabit physical bodies will do so, as it is stated: “For the spirit that enwraps itself is from Me, and the souls that I have made” (Isaiah 57:16). Consequently, once a child has been born and his soul has entered a body the mitzva has been fulfilled, even if the child subsequently dies. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said he has not fulfilled the mitzva, as we require “He formed it to be inhabited” (Isaiah 45:18), and this is not fulfilled when the children have passed away and no longer inhabit the earth.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Beit Yaakov on Torah, Chayei Sara 17:1: “This is the secret of doubling: through it God builds a double good. Afterward the person will no longer need such extraordinary fear, and God will also give him double reward for having had such great fear until now. If God showed him only what would be from now onward, and not concerning the past, he would still have no rest about the past—why he had needed to be in such great fear. h: Wine and spiritual joy and the inner life of the soul

p: וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן דְּכָל כַּמָּה דְּלָא שָׁתֵינָא רְבִיעֲתָא דְּחַמְרָא לָא צִילָאי דַּעְתַּאי,
And likewise that which Rav Nachman stated, that as long as he had not drunk a revi'it of wine his mind was not settled,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל שֶׁנִּצְרַךְ הַיַּיִן לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב וּלְשַׂמְּחוֹ,
is also after the fall, when wine became necessary to straighten the heart and gladden it,
וְקוֹדֶם הָעִרְבּוּב טוֹב וָרָע לֹא הָיָה נִצְרַךְ הַיַּיִן כְּלָל.
whereas before the mixing of good and evil wine was not needed whatsoever.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, Rosh Hashanah 47:1: “This is also what the Sages said concerning the cup of blessing: a person must set his eyes upon it, and all sanctifications are recited specifically over a cup of wine. The cup of blessing also alludes to the attribute of the kingdom of Heaven, which has no eyes; therefore one must set one’s eyes upon it—that is, look deeply and bring eyes into it. The commandment is specifically with wine because wine makes a person forget his understanding. When a person looks deeply and brings eyes into the cup of wine, he will find in this very wine the joy of a commandment.”

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Et HaOchel 1:1: “Oil, which alludes to wisdom—the clear knowledge and recognition that “I am your God”—comes after proper eating, as is fitting for God’s sake, to sustain one’s soul. Then it adds wisdom and knowledge of God afterward. Gross eating like an animal, however, dulls the heart and mind. Thus the Sages said: “The reason I did not tell you … was that I had not eaten beef.””

h: The Gemara’s teaching and spiritual perfection

p: וְכֵן אַחַר שֶׁסּוֹעֵד, דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יב עַמּוּד ב):
And so too after dining, as brought in the Gemara (Bava Batra 12b):
"אַחַר שֶׁאוֹכֵל וְשׁוֹתֶה אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא לֵב אֶחָד",
''After one eats and drinks he possesses only one heart,''
וְלֹא נִתְפָּרֵשׁ אֵיזֶה לֵב אֶחָד,
and it was not specified which one heart;
שֶׁמִּקּוֹדֶם שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי לְבָבוֹת, הַיְינוּ יֵצֶר טוֹב וְיֵצֶר רָע,
for beforehand he has two hearts—the good inclination and the evil inclination—
וּלְאַחַר שֶׁאָכַל וְשָׁתָה, אִם הָיְתָה אֲכִילָתוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה,
and after eating and drinking, if his eating was conducted in holiness,
יֵשׁ לוֹ רַק לֵב אֶחָד לַאֲבִיהוּ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
he possesses solely one heart directed toward his Father in Heaven,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה מְתַקֵּן הַפְּגָם שֶׁהָיָה בָּאֲכִילָה;
since through sanctified eating he rectifies the primordial defect incurred through eating;
וְאִם חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הָאֲכִילָה לְשֵׁם תַּאֲוָה,
but if, Heaven forbid, eating was for physical lust,
אָז עַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילָה גּוֹרֵם קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע,
then through that eating he incites the accusation of the evil inclination,
שֶׁאֵין יֵצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ בְּסִפְרֵי מִכַּמָּה פְסוּקִים.
for the evil inclination dominates only out of eating and drinking, as expounded in the Sifrei from multiple verses.
וְעַל יְדֵי בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן שֶׁמְּבָרֵךְ אַחַר אֲכִילָתוֹ פּוֹעֵל שֶׁלֹּא יַזִּיק אֲכִילָתוֹ,
And through the Grace after Meals recited following eating, he effects that his food not cause harm,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁמַּכִּיר כֹּחַ הַנּוֹתֵן,
since he recognizes the power of the Giver,
וּכְשֶׁבָּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אֵינוֹ גוֹרֵם קִטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע.
and when acknowledged as from Hashem, it does not induce the accusation of the evil inclination.
וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נג עַמּוּד ב):
And so they expounded (Berakhot 53b):
"'וְהִתְקַדִּשְׁתֶּם' – אֵלּוּ מַיִם רִאשׁוֹנִים, 'וִהְיִיתֶם קְדֹשִׁים' – אֵלּוּ מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים וְכוּלֵי",
''And you shall sanctify yourselves'—these are the initial waters (netilat yadayim); 'and you shall be holy'—these are the final waters (mayim acharonim), etc.,'
וְכָל זֶה עֵצָה שֶׁתִּהְיֶה הָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָׁה.
and all this is counsel so that eating be enveloped in sanctity.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 12b: ‘Having already cited one statement of Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa, the Gemara cites another statement in his name: Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa says: Before a person eats and drinks he has two hearts, meaning his heart is unsettled because he is distracted by hunger. But after he eats and drinks he has only one heart, as it is stated: “A hollow [nevuv] man is two-hearted” (Job 11:12). How is it indicated that “nevuv” means hungry? As it is written concerning the altar: “Nevuv luḥot” (Exodus 27:8), which we translate into Aramaic as: Hollow with planks, meaning that a hollow person, i.e., one who has not yet eaten, is two-hearted.’

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 53b: ‘Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said of this: I do not know of Zilai or Zivai or Zuhamai; rather, I know a baraita, as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said, and some say that it was taught in a baraita: It is stated: “And you shall sanctify yourselves, and you shall be holy, for holy am I, the Lord your God” (Leviticus 20:26). With regard to this verse, the Sages said: And you shall sanctify yourselves, these are the first waters with which one washes his hands before the meal; and you shall be holy, these are the final waters; for holy, this is oil which one spreads on his hands; am I, the Lord your God, this is the Grace after Meals blessing.’

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Emor 3: “Thus the Talmud states: Rabbi Levi raised a contradiction: it is written, “The earth and its fullness belong to the Lord,” and it is written, “He has given the earth to human beings.” There is no difficulty: one is before a blessing, the other after a blessing. “After a blessing” indicates that the person recognizes God is the giver of the good and the good remains in His hand. This is what a blessing indicates. Then the person has a complete acquisition of the good, and it is called, “He has given the earth to human beings.””

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Et HaOchel 9:1: “This is the meaning of what is written in Eruvin: “Snatch and eat ... for it resembles a wedding feast.” This world is the union of groom and bride: a person’s receiving bounty from the blessed God. This occurs only in this world, where a person’s work involves awakening from below and desire, and he receives in response an awakening from above and the fulfillment of the masculine waters. This is the wedding. “The reward of a wedding feast is words”: as the Sages said in the chapter Helek, “Man is born to toil”—the toil of the mouth in Torah and prayer. Through this they gladden groom and bride, arousing feminine waters through prayer’s awakening from below and masculine waters from above through Torah. Thereby a person also effects unifications in eating: he apprehends the presence of the blessed God as the One who gives life. Through this he “snatches and eats,” seizing those oppressed sparks into holiness. Therefore tractate Nazir, whose concern is setting bounds to desires, ends with “Snatch and bless.” Those who fear God and set bounds to their desires are given this power of seizing. Hence “and bless”: the Grace after Meals, thanking the blessed God when one is satisfied, completes the act of seizing.”

sourceExcerpt.en: This is the meaning of what is written in Eruvin: “Snatch and eat ... for it resembles a wedding feast.” This world is the union of groom and bride: a person’s receiving bounty from the blessed God. paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Et HaOchel 6:1: “The table resembles the altar, as stated at the end of Chagigah. Conversely, Avot speaks of “sacrifices of the dead,” meaning offerings to idolatry, as the expression is explained in Psalms and in the first chapter of Hullin. When a person’s enjoyment of food enters the divine soul, the portion of God from above within him, this means that he recognizes that the blessed God created this food, gives it life, existence, and endurance, gives it flavor and enjoyment, and gives the person the desire to want it, taste its goodness, and increase his strength and vitality. When he clearly recognizes that all this comes from God, with a recognition shining in the heart—without deceiving himself by treating a merely passing imagined thought as clear recognition—this recognition comes from the divine portion and the good within him. That side grows stronger, and its enjoyment is truly like the enjoyment of the offering above, for the part is equivalent to the whole. But when he forgets this and eats for his own pleasure to fulfill desire, it comes from the person’s desiring animal soul, as though he offered a sacrifice to it. These are truly “sacrifices of the dead.” This power and desire accord with the saying that the wicked are called dead in their lives: the apparent life is only an image, while in truth it is death. Its offering is “sacrifices of the dead” and an offering to idolatry, for this is idolatry: forgetting God and filling a power other than God’s power. The counsel is a table with words of Torah upon it. Torah’s light brings the clarification by which one recognizes that it comes from God, for wisdom means recognition. This is also the purpose of the blessing the Sages instituted before eating: to recognize that God creates and brings this food into existence as food.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: הַשֻּׁלְחָן דּוֹמֶה לַמִּזְבֵּחַ כִּדְאִיתָא בְּשִׁלְהֵי חֲגִיגָה [כ״ז עַמּוּד א׳], וּבְהֵיפֶךְ אָמַר בְּאָבוֹת [פֶּרֶק ג׳ מִשְׁנָה ג׳]: "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים", דְּהַיְינוּ תִּקְרֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, כִּמְפֹרָשׁ בִּתְהִלִּים [ק״ו:כ״ח] דְּנִקְרָא "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים", וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּחֻלִּין [י״ג עַמּוּד ב׳]. וְהַיְינוּ כִּי הַהֲנָאָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָאָדָם מִן הַמַּאֲכָל, אִם נִכְנֶסֶת לַנֶּפֶשׁ הָאֱלֹהִית וְחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ מִמַּעַל שֶׁבּוֹ, הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא מַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בָּרָא אֶת הַמַּאֲכָל הַזֶּה וּמְחַיֵּהוּ וְנוֹתֵן לוֹ הֲוָיָה וְקִיּוּם, וְהוּא נוֹתֵן בּוֹ טַעַם וַהֲנָאָה, וְנוֹתֵן לָאָדָם חֵשֶׁק שֶׁיִּתְאַוֶּה לוֹ וְשֶׁיִּטְעַם בּוֹ טַעַם טוֹב וְשֶׁיּוֹסִיף בְּכֹחוֹ וְחִיּוּתוֹ; כְּשֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁזֶּה הַכֹּל מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה, מֵאִיר בַּלֵּב בְּלִי הַטְעָיָה בְּנַפְשׁוֹ לַחְשֹׁב דִּמְיוֹן דֶּרֶךְ הַעֲבָרָה בְּעָלְמָא, לְהַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה הִנֵּה הַכָּרָה זוֹ הוּא מִכֹּחַ הַחֵלֶק אֱלוֹהַּ וְצַד הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ, וְאוֹתוֹ הַצַּד נִתְגַּבֵּר, וַהֲנָאַת אוֹתוֹ הַצַּד הוּא מַמָּשׁ הֲנָאַת הַקָּרְבָּן שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה, כִּי שָׁוֶה הוּא הַחֵלֶק עִם הַכֹּל. אֲבָל כְּשֶׁשּׁוֹכֵחַ זֶה וְאוֹכֵל לַהֲנָאַת עַצְמוֹ לְמִלּוּי הַתַּאֲוָה, זֶהוּ מִצַּד נֶפֶשׁ הַמִּתְאַוָּה הַבְּהֵמִית שֶׁבָּאָדָם, וּכְאִלּוּ מַקְרִיב לָהּ קָרְבָּן; וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן כַּוָּנַת הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים קֹדֶם אֲכִילָה, שֶׁעִנְיָנָהּ הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַבּוֹרֵא וּמְהַוֶּה מַאֲכָל זֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַאֲכָל.

וְזֶהוּ "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים" מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁכֹּחַ זֶה וְתַאֲוָה זוֹ הוּא כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: רְשָׁעִים בְּחַיֵּיהֶם קְרוּיִים מֵתִים, שֶׁהַחִיּוּת הוּא דִּמְיוֹן בְּעָלְמָא אֲבָל בֶּאֱמֶת הוּא מִיתָה, וְהַקְרָבָתָהּ הוּא "זִבְחֵי מֵתִים" וְתִקְרֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה: הַשִּׁכְחָה מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִלּוּי כֹּחַ אַחֵר חוּץ מִכֹּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְהָעֵצָה לָזֶה הוּא שֻׁלְחָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהַמָּאוֹר שֶׁבָּהּ הוּא הַמְבָרֵר שֶׁמַּכִּיר שֶׁהוּא מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי חָכְמָה לְשׁוֹן הַכָּרָה כַּיָּדוּעַ; וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן כַּוָּנַת הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁתִּקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים קֹדֶם אֲכִילָה, שֶׁעִנְיָנָהּ הַהַכָּרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַבּוֹרֵא וּמְהַוֶּה מַאֲכָל זֶה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מַאֲכָל.
sourceExcerpt.en: The table resembles the altar, as stated at the end of Chagigah. Conversely, Avot speaks of “sacrifices of the dead,” meaning offerings to idolatry, as the expression is explained in Psalms and in the first chapter of Hullin. When a person’s enjoyment of food enters the divine soul, the portion of God from above within him, this means that he recognizes that the blessed God created this food, gives it life, existence, and endurance, gives it flavor and enjoyment, and gives the person the desire to want it, taste its goodness, and increase his strength and vitality. When he clearly recognizes that all this comes from God, with a recognition shining in the heart—without deceiving himself by treating a merely passing imagined thought as clear recognition—this recognition comes from the divine portion and the good within him. That side grows stronger, and its enjoyment is truly like the enjoyment of the offering above, for the part is equivalent to the whole. But when he forgets this and eats for his own pleasure to fulfill desire, it comes from the person’s desiring animal soul, as though he offered a sacrifice to it. These are truly “sacrifices of the dead.” This power and desire accord with the saying that the wicked are called dead in their lives: the apparent life is only an image, while in truth it is death. Its offering is “sacrifices of the dead” and an offering to idolatry, for this is idolatry: forgetting God and filling a power other than God’s power. The counsel is a table with words of Torah upon it. Torah’s light brings the clarification by which one recognizes that it comes from God, for wisdom means recognition. This is also the purpose of the blessing the Sages instituted before eating: to recognize that God creates and brings this food into existence as food.

h: Gladness for the upright in heart

p: וּלְזֶה הַמִּצְוָה לְבָרֵךְ עַל כּוֹס יַיִן לְשַׂמֵּחַ הַלֵּב, לִהְיוֹת "לִישְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה",
And toward this goal is the mitzvah to bless over a cup of wine to gladden the heart, so there be 'gladness for the upright in heart,'
וְהַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל וּלְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב.
meaning when one merits to empty evil from the foolish heart and straighten it.
וּבַגְּמָרָא (עֲרָכִין יא עַמּוּד א):
And in the Gemara (Arachin 11a):
"אֵיזוֹהִי עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְטוּב לֵבָב? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה שִׁירָה",
''Which is service that is with joy and goodness of heart? Say: this is song,''
וְאָמְרוּ שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן וְכוּלֵי,
and they stated that song is uttered only over wine, etc.,
וְהַיְינוּ "בְּטוּב לֵבָב" – שְׁנֵי הַלְּבָבוֹת,
and this 'goodness of heart' refers to both hearts,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ: "'בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ' – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ, בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע וּבְיֵצֶר טוֹב",
as they expounded: ''With all your heart'—with both your inclinations, with the evil inclination and with the good inclination,'
וְזֶהוּ טוּב לֵבָב, כְּשֶׁזּוֹכִין לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֵב אֶחָד לְטוֹבָה.
and that is genuine goodness of heart, when one merits to align the heart so it is singular for good.

paragraphs.text: Arakhin 11a: ‘Rav Mattana said that the source for the requirement to accompany the Temple offerings with song is derived from here: “Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joyfulness, and with goodness of heart” (Deuteronomy 28:47). What is this service of God that is performed with joyfulness and with goodness of heart? You must say that this is song. The Gemara objects: But you can say that this service is studying the words of Torah, as it is written: “The precepts of the Lord are upright, rejoicing the heart” (Psalms 19:9). The Gemara explains: Torah is indeed called a matter that rejoices the heart, but it is not called “goodness.”’

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Rav Tzadok · Tzidkat HaTzadik 102:1: “One who conducts himself in holiness even in all permitted matters and bodily needs—that is, all his actions are for Heaven, and he brings God’s service and will into them, as the Sages said concerning Hillel and Shammai—is called a hasid, a pious person. That means he does not merely adhere to the strict line of law. This is “With all your heart”—with both your inclinations. A righteous person subdues his inclination, but this person brings holiness also into all the inclination’s desires. Then God, measure for measure, places holiness in all he does, and he merits to bring forth much holiness specifically from the evil inclination. It is then called “very good,” more than simply good. Concerning this it says, “Where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot ….” God arranges missteps and obstacles for him, and he needs repentance and atonement for them, for they are called sin; through this he brings the precious forth from the base.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: מִי שֶׁמִּתְנַהֵג אֲפִילּוּ בְּכָל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת וְצָרְכֵי גּוּפָנִיִּים בִּקְדוּשָׁה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וּמַכְנִיס בָּהֶם עַבְדוּת וּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בֵּיצָה טז.) בְּהִלֵּל וְשַׁמַּאי – זֶהוּ נִקְרָא "חָסִיד", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלָּאו דַּוְקָא מְדַקְדֵּק עַל פִּי שׁוּרַת הַדִּין. וְזֶה נִקְרָא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁצַּדִּיק הוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ, אֲבָל זֶה מַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה גַּם בְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת הַיֵּצֶר; וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה נוֹתֵן קְדוּשָׁה בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה, וְזוֹכֶה לְהוֹצִיא קְדוּשָׁה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע דַּיְיקָא; וְאָז נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד", שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר מִטּוֹב סְתָם; וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים וְכוּלֵי. וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ תַּקָּלוֹת וּמִכְשׁוֹלִים, וְהוּא צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה וְכַפָּרָה עַל זֶה דְּנִקְרָא חֵטְא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל.

sourceExcerpt.he: מִי שֶׁמִּתְנַהֵג אֲפִילּוּ בְּכָל דִּבְרֵי הָרְשׁוּת וְצָרְכֵי גּוּפָנִיִּים בִּקְדוּשָׁה, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁכָּל מַעֲשָׂיו לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וּמַכְנִיס בָּהֶם עַבְדוּת וּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בֵּיצָה טז.) בְּהִלֵּל וְשַׁמַּאי – זֶהוּ נִקְרָא "חָסִיד", רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלָּאו דַּוְקָא מְדַקְדֵּק עַל פִּי שׁוּרַת הַדִּין. וְזֶה נִקְרָא "בְּכָל לְבָבְךָ" – בִּשְׁנֵי יְצָרֶיךָ וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁצַּדִּיק הוּא הַכּוֹבֵשׁ יִצְרוֹ, אֲבָל זֶה מַכְנִיס קְדוּשָׁה גַּם בְּכָל חֶמְדּוֹת הַיֵּצֶר; וְאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִדָּה כְּנֶגֶד מִדָּה נוֹתֵן קְדוּשָׁה בְּכָל מַה שֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה, וְזוֹכֶה לְהוֹצִיא קְדוּשָׁה הַרְבֵּה מִן הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע דַּיְיקָא; וְאָז נִקְרָא "טוֹב מְאֹד", שֶׁהוּא יוֹתֵר מִטּוֹב סְתָם; וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבַּעֲלֵי תְשׁוּבָה עוֹמְדִין אֵין צַדִּיקִים גְּמוּרִים וְכוּלֵי. וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לוֹ תַּקָּלוֹת וּמִכְשׁוֹלִים, וְהוּא צָרִיךְ תְּשׁוּבָה וְכַפָּרָה עַל זֶה דְּנִקְרָא חֵטְא, וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל.
sourceExcerpt.en: One who conducts himself in holiness even in all permitted matters and bodily needs—that is, all his actions are for Heaven, and he brings God’s service and will into them, as the Sages said concerning Hillel and Shammai—is called a hasid, a pious person. That means he does not merely adhere to the strict line of law. This is “With all your heart”—with both your inclinations. A righteous person subdues his inclination, but this person brings holiness also into all the inclination’s desires. Then God, measure for measure, places holiness in all he does, and he merits to bring forth much holiness specifically from the evil inclination. It is then called “very good,” more than simply good. Concerning this it says, “Where penitents stand, the wholly righteous cannot ….” God arranges missteps and obstacles for him, and he needs repentance and atonement for them, for they are called sin; through this he brings the precious forth from the base.

h: The written and oral Torah and wine and spiritual joy

p: וְכֵן מִצְוַת נְסָכִים מוֹרָה שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשִׂמְחָה וְנִיחָא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
And likewise the commandment of libations demonstrates that Hashem is in joy and serenity from Israel,
וְזֶה נִצְרַךְ רַק אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל;
and this became necessary only after the fall;
אֲבָל קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל לֹא נִצְרְכוּ כְּלָל לְקָרְבָּנוֹת,
for prior to the fall, sacrifices were not needed at all,
שֶׁהֲרֵי קָרְבָּן רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁהִקְרִיב אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הָיָה רַק אַחַר שֶׁאָמַר:
since the very first sacrifice that Adam offered was only after he lamented:
"שֶׁבִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁסָּרַחְתִּי עוֹלָם חָשַׁךְ בַּעֲדִי וְכוּלֵי, כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר וְכוּלֵי עָמַד וְהִקְרִיב וְכוּלֵי",
''Because I sinned the world is darkened before me, etc.; once dawn arose, etc., he stood and offered, etc.,''
וְכֵן נֹחַ הִקְרִיב הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת אַחַר הַמַּבּוּל.
and similarly Noach offered sacrifices after the Flood.
וּלְעָתִיד כָּל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת בְּטֵלִין, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ט),
And in the ultimate future all sacrifices will be nullified, as written (Vayikra Rabbah 9),
וְקָרְבַּן תּוֹדָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּטֵל הוּא גַּם כֵּן לְהוֹדוֹת עַל נֵס שֶׁנִּיצוֹל מִצָּרָה;
and the Thanksgiving offering which is never nullified is likewise to give thanks over a miracle of being saved from distress;
וְקוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ כְּלָל קָרְבָּן,
and prior to the fall, no sacrifice was needed at all,
וְלֹא הָיָה נְסָכִים כְּלָל,
nor were there any libations,
הַנְּסָכִים בָּאוּ רַק לְהָבִיא שִׂמְחָה.
libations arriving solely to usher in joy.
כִּי כְּשֶׁהָאָדָם מַר נֶפֶשׁ, כִּבְיָכוֹל אֵין הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּנִיחָא,
For when man is embittered in soul, as it were Hashem is not in serenity,
וְאַחַר שֶׁמְּתַקֵּן מֵבִיא נְסָכִים שֶׁאָז הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּנִיחָא;
and after he rectifies he brings libations, whereupon Hashem is in serenity;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל לֹא הָיָה נִצְרַךְ כְּלָל לְיַיִן,
unlike prior to the fall when wine was not needed at all,
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא יַיִן רַק לְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים וְכוּלֵי".
and this is what they meant: 'Wine was created only to comfort mourners, etc.'

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Sod Yesharim, The First Day of Pesach 1:2: “The holy Zohar says concerning offerings that the will of the offering reaches to the Infinite. Nevertheless, the essential service follows the Sages’ statement: “For the sake of the Name … for the sake of the One who spoke and the world came to be.” That is, it is directed to the Creator’s will, which desired the world’s existence and these garments. Service does not apply to the Infinite, the place that cannot be known. Rather, we serve for the satisfaction of the One who spoke and whose will was done: we perform this service because He commanded it and this is His will in these garments. Therefore we serve Him through these garments. In truth, from His own side God does not need any of these garments.”

h: Wine and spiritual joy and the inner life of the soul — the holiness of Israel

p: וְזֶהוּ "בְּחַמְרָא גּוֹ כָסָא" – שֶׁהוּא לְיַשֵּׁר הַלֵּב וּלְשַׂמְּחוֹ,
And this is 'with wine in the cup'—which serves to straighten the heart and gladden it,
"וּמְדָאנֵי אָסָא" – שֶׁבָּאוּ לְהוֹרוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
and 'bundles of myrtle'—which come to point regarding Israel that which is stated: 'And your people are all righteous,'
כֵּיוָן דְּאִתְגְּזַר אִקְרֵי צַדִּיק.
since once circumcised he is titled righteous.
וְעַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת אֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֶּאֱנוֹשׁ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ;
And through the observance of Shabbat, even if one served idols like the generation of Enosh he is forgiven;
וּבַמְּכִילְתָּא: "'שֹׁמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשֹׁמֵר יָדוֹ וְגוֹמֵר' – שֶׁהַמְשַׁמֵּר שַׁבָּת מְשׁוּמָּר מִן הָעֲבֵירָה",
and in the Mekhilta: ''He who guards the Sabbath from profaning it and keeps his hand, etc.'—whoever guards Shabbat is preserved from sin,'
וּבִפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים: שֶׁנִּיצוֹל מִקִּטְרוּג הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
and in Pri Etz Chayyim: that he is rescued from the accusation of the evil inclination,
בְּוַדַּאי כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל צַדִּיקִים.
certainly all Israel are righteous.
וְזֶהוּ "לַאֲרוּס וַאֲרוּסָה לְאִתְקָפָא חַלָּשִׁין" –
And this is 'for the groom and bride to strengthen the weak'—
מַה שֶּׁחָלַשׁ דַּעְתָּם מִימֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה שֶׁעָבְרוּ בְּטִרְדּוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
strengthening their faint spirits from the weekdays spent in worldly preoccupations,
וְעַל יְדֵי הַיַּיִן קִדּוּשׁ וּמְדָאנֵי אָסָא נִתְחַזֵּק וּמִתְיַישֵּׁר הַלֵּב.
and through the wine of Kiddush and bundles of myrtle, the heart is reinforced and aligned in uprightness.

paragraphs.text: Kisvei Ishbitz–Radzin · Tiferet Yosef, Hoshana Rabba 2: ““A branch of a thick-leaved tree” indicates what the Midrash says: it has fragrance but no taste. Taste indicates a place where everything is already clarified for good. This, however, indicates that it is not yet clarified, but is destined to be clarified. A good person is given a taste of the fruits of his deeds in this world, but this person [represented by the myrtle] does not yet experience taste in his service. This is what having fragrance indicates, as the Talmud says: “What is something the soul enjoys but the body does not? Fragrance.” Since an Israelite has a divine portion from above, he will certainly eventually be clarified for good. At present, however, he is not yet clarified. Where everything is clarified for good is indicated by the etrog; the branch of a thick-leaved tree indicates that he is not yet entirely clarified for good.”

reviewedSourceExcerpt.he: וענף עץ עבות מורה, כמו דאיתא במדרש (רבה אמור ל') שיש בו ריח ולא טעם. טעם מורה במקום שכבר מבורר כולו לטוב, אבל זה מורה שאין עדיין מבורר, ורק עתיד להתברר ולאדם טוב מטעימין לו מפרי מעשיו בעוה"ז, אבל שירגיש טעם בעבודתו אין לו עדיין. וזה מורה שיש לו ריח, כמו שאיתא בש"ס (ברכות מ"ג:) איזה דבר שהנשמה נהנת ממנו ולא הגוף, הוי אומר זה הריח, והיינו מאחר שבישראל יש בו חלק אלהי ממעל, ממילא בטח עתיד להתברר לטוב, אבל לעת עתה אינו מבורר עדיין, כי במקום שהוא מבורר כולו לטוב, זה מורה אתרוג. אבל ענף עץ עבות, מורה שאינו מבורר עדיין כולו לטוב.
